math_review.definitions: T_P(x) = x - P G(x) on closed Euclidean ball B_2(x_c, r). P is required to be non-singular so that P G(x*) = 0 iff G(x*) = 0.
assumptions: G is an exact canonical multivariate polynomial map with binary64 coefficients.
P is an invertible diagonal preconditioner with non-zero finite entries.
B_2(x_c, r) is enclosed in outward box product_i [x_{c,i} - r, x_{c,i} + r].
Matrix 2-norm is upper-bounded by Frobenius norm.
math_review.derivation: q_hi >= sup_{x in B} ||I - P DG(x)||_2 with q_hi < 1; rho_hi >= ||P G(x_c)||_2 with rho_hi <= mul_down(sub_down(1.0, q_hi), r). Banach fixed-point theorem proves unique root in B_2(x_c, r) with root error bounded by div_up(rho_hi, sub_down(1.0, q_hi)).
math_review.roundoff_model: Directed outward interval arithmetic (IEEE-754 next_up / next_down via rodas5p_core::directed).
